candidates.description: User-supplied query parameter `q` is directly interpolated into a raw SQL SELECT statement without parameterization or escaping, allowing arbitrary SQL execution.
candidates.rationale: `criteria` is assigned from `req.query.q` (line 21-22) then interpolated into a template literal passed to `sequelize.query()` (line 23). No parameterized binding or escaping is applied. Verification: send a crafted `q` value like `' UNION SELECT ...` and observe whether the response reflects injected data or causes a SQL error.
candidates.title: SQL injection via unparameterized query in searchProducts

candidates.description: User-supplied `orderLinesData` from the request body is evaluated inside a Node.js VM context via `safeEval`, which is a known-bypass sandbox for `notevil`.
candidates.rationale: `body.orderLinesData` (line 19) is placed into a VM sandbox and executed via `vm.runInContext('safeEval(orderLinesData)', sandbox)` (line 23). The `notevil` library has documented escape vectors. The route is protected by `security.isAuthorized()` so any authenticated user can reach this sink. Verification: submit a payload that triggers a detectable side-effect (e.g., a timing delay or error message difference) without destructive operations.
candidates.title: Server-side code injection via vm.runInContext with user-controlled input

candidates.description: The placeOrder handler uses `req.body.UserId` to decrement and increment wallet balances without verifying the authenticated user owns that wallet.
candidates.rationale: Lines 146-162 read `req.body.UserId` and perform `WalletModel.decrement` and `WalletModel.increment` on that user's wallet. The authenticated user identity is only used for the email in the PDF (line 38-39), never compared to `req.body.UserId`. An attacker can specify another user's ID to drain or inflate their wallet. Verification: authenticate as user A, submit an order with `UserId` set to user B's ID, and check if user B's wallet balance changes.
candidates.title: Missing ownership check allows wallet manipulation via arbitrary UserId in placeOrder
